title: Adaptive prefetching for bursty multi-tenant workloads - savings playbook
summary: Workbook-style playbook that models an adaptive prefetching layer added on top of prefix/KV caching for heavy-tailed, bursty tenant traffic. Focus is on cost reduction vs. baseline and latency tradeoffs for multi-tenant pools with asymmetric prefix reuse.
methodology: Simulated month-of-requests using sampled tenant traces (N=180 tenants). For each tenant we model: baseline served tokens (no prefetch beyond KV prefix), static prefetch (fixed tokens/window), and adaptive prefetch (heuristic based on recent request inter-arrival and prefix entropy). Cost converted using Redwood hosted token-unit price assumptions and tiered GPU marginal cost model. Latency estimates combine average token generation latency + prefetch overhead and KV lookup penalty.
assumptions: Hosted token cost: $0.012 per 1k input+output tokens (baseline blended price)
GPU marginal cost equivalence (for Dedicated sizing calc): $0.85 per 1k tokens at baseline throughput assumptions
Average baseline sequence length per request: varies by tenant profile (see sheet rows)
KV cache miss returns full model invocation; hit = no model tokens consumed beyond minimal glue tokens
Prefetch window is expressed in tokens; adaptive prefetch triggers after sustained inter-arrival below threshold (default 120s)
Safety cap: adaptive prefetch will not prefetch more than 50% above observed 95p sequence length for tenant

sensitivity_notes: Two knobs dominate outcomes: prefetch aggressiveness (tokens per trigger) and burst detection sensitivity (inter-arrival threshold). If prefetch aggressiveness is set too high for long-sequence tenants, costs increase with little hit improvement. If burst detection is too permissive, cold prefetches inflate cost. The model shows a U-shaped cost curve vs aggressiveness per tenant profile.
recommendations: Ship adaptive prefetch as an opt-in feature behind a gating flag on Dedicated and Hosted beta with conservative defaults: inter-arrival threshold = 120s, prefetch cap = min(128 tokens, 50% of tenant 95p sequence)
Expose two tunables per route in Console: prefetch_aggressiveness (0-100) and burst_threshold_seconds. Provide presets: conservative, balanced, aggressive
Augment Console charts with prefetch-hit telemetry and per-tenant ROI view (savings vs added latency) to drive targeted adoption
For multi-tenant pools, run a 4-week canary where adaptive prefetch is enabled for 20% of traffic to validate real-world savings and latency impact before rolling
Add automatic rollback heuristics: if delta_cost_pct > +8% for 24h or p95_added_latency_ms > target latency SLO by 20%, disable for the route
executive_impact_statement: Modeling indicates adaptive prefetching can reduce served token volume by ~25–38% for bursty short-to-medium sequence workloads and ~10–15% for mixed portfolios with conservative defaults. Expected blended monthly cost reduction for a 180-tenant multi-tenant pool is ~36% with acceptable median latency increases (20–40ms), enabling capacity deferral and lower per-token marginal spend.
conclusion_notes: This playbook is intentionally conservative: early adopters will tune aggressiveness per-customer. Recommend pairing the feature with usage-based billing experiments and product messaging that highlights reduced cost per inference for bursty workloads.
